name: nano
one_line: small friendly text editor for the terminal
plain: `nano` is a simple text editor that runs in the terminal. You just type; the commands are shown at the bottom of the screen, where ^ means the Ctrl key (^X is Ctrl+X).
It is the easy way to edit a config file, a script or a note on a server without learning vim.
when: Edit a config file or script on a server.
Write a quick note or a payload file.
Open a file at a certain line.
Edit files with line numbers shown.

examples.title: Open or create a file
examples.explain: If it does not exist it is created when you save. Type, then Ctrl+O (write out) and Enter to save, Ctrl+X to exit.

examples.title: Edit a system file
examples.explain: Files owned by root need sudo, or nano says it cannot write.

examples.title: Jump to a line when opening
examples.explain: +42 opens with the cursor on line 42. +42,10 also sets the column.

examples.title: Search and replace
examples.cmd: Ctrl+W to search, Ctrl+\ to replace
examples.explain: Type the old text, Enter, then the new text, then A to replace all or Y/N for each match.

examples.title: Cut and paste lines
examples.cmd: Ctrl+K cut the line, Ctrl+U paste it
examples.explain: Cut several lines in a row to move a block. Ctrl+6 (or Alt+A) marks the start of a selection.

examples.title: Undo and redo
examples.explain: Fix a mistake without leaving the file.

examples.title: Read another file in
examples.cmd: Ctrl+R, type a file name, Enter
examples.explain: Inserts the contents of that file at the cursor.

examples.title: Safe editing
examples.explain: -B saves a backup file important.conf~ when you write.

options.plain: Start with the cursor at this line and column.
Indent new lines like the previous one.
Wrap long lines on screen only.
Save a backup of the old file when writing.
Restricted mode: no reading or writing other files, no shell.
Home key goes to the first text, not column 0.
Do not add a newline at the end of the file.
Use bold instead of reverse video for the title bar.
Hide the shortcut list at the bottom.
Help, show cursor position, go to line.

mistakes: Closing with Ctrl+X and answering N by accident: you lose changes. Answer Y then Enter to save.
Editing a file you lack write permission to: use sudo.
Terminal wrap adding invisible line breaks in long commands: use -w.
Pasting tabs or spaces into a YAML file and breaking it: use -E.
Not noticing nano added a trailing newline when the exact bytes matter (-L).
try: Create a file, type three lines, save and exit.
Open it at line 2 with nano +2.
Cut one line and paste it two lines lower.
see_also: vim(1), vi(1), sed(1), less(1), cat(1), tee(1), and nano's own help with Ctrl+G.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
